pride_data.title: DSSBU: novel cross-linker tested on bovine serum albumin and human hemoglobin
pride_data.projectDescription: Protein cross-linking has assumed an irreplaceable role in structural proteomics. Recently, significant efforts have been made to develop novel MS-cleavable reagents. These cross-linkers enhance the reliability of cross-link identification. Presently, only water-insoluble MS-cleavable cross-linkers are commercially available. However, the comprehensive analysis of the various chemical and structural motifs inherent in proteins depends on the targeting of different protein sites with varying degrees of hydrophilicity. We introduce a new MS-cleavable cross-linker called disulfodisuccinimidyl dibutyric urea (DSSBU), which we have developed in-house. DSSBU contains an N-hydroxysulfosuccinimide (sulfo-NHS) reactive group. It therefore serves as a water-soluble counterpart to the commercially available and widely used disuccinimidyl dibutyric urea (DSBU). To investigate the applicability of DSSBU, we compared the efficacy of four similar cross-linkers—bis[sulfosuccinimidyl] suberate (BS3), disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS), DSBU and DSSBU on bovine serum albumin. We also compared efficacy of DSBU and DSSBU on human hemoglobin. Our results demonstrate that the superior water solubility of DSSBU enables to avoid the usage of polar solvents such as DMSO but still maintaining the effectivity of MS-cleavable crosslinker such as DSBU.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein Cross-Linking BSA (purchased from Merck, product no. A2153) was  treated with BS3, DSSBU, DSS and DSBU cross-linkers by the usage of 50- and 100-fold molar excess concentrations of the cross-linkers to BSA. The cross-linkers were dissolved in water (BS3 and DSSBU), in DMSO (DSS and DSBU), and DMSO containing 2% of water (BS3, DSSBU, DSS and DSBU). To cross-link by the DSBU and DSSBU mixture, DSBU and DSSBU were dissolved in DMSO containing 2% of water and mixed in the molar ratio of 1:1 (50-fold molar excess of both cross-linkers) and 1:2 (50-fold molar excess of DSBU and 100-fold molar excess of DSSBU). Hemoglobin (purchased from Merck, product no. H7379) was  treated with DSBU, DSSBU and their mixture. DSSBU and DSBU were dissolved in DMSO containing 2% of water and applied in 20- and 40-fold molar excesses to hemoglobin separately or were mixed in equimolar ratio for both excesses.  One microlitre of a freshly prepared stock solution of each cross-linker was added to 30 µl of a 10 µM BSA solution or to 14 µl of 25 µM hemoglobin solution, both dissolved in 20 mM of HEPES buffer (pH 8). All reaction mixtures were then incubated for 30 min at 25°C. The reaction was quenched by the addition of a 1 M tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (tris) buffer solution (pH 8.8) in a volume sufficient to obtain a 50-fold molar excess of tris over the cross-linker. The resulting mixture was further incubated for 15 min. In-Solution Digestion of the Cross-Linked Protein One microlitre of a 100 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) solution was added to 20 µl of the cross-linked reaction mixture, resulting in a final concentration of 5 mM. The mixture was incubated at 65°C for 30 min and then cooled. Subsequently, 2 µl of a 100 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) solution was added to achieve a final concentration of 15 mM. The mixture was then incubated at room temperature in the dark for 30 min. This was followed by the addition of 2 µl of a 100 mM DTT solution. Samples were digested by Pierce MS-grade trypsin protease (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with an enzyme-to-protein ratio of 1:50 (w/w) at 37°C for 16 h. The digested peptide mixtures were dried down and resuspended in 100 µl of a solvent containing 5% acetonitrile (ACN) and 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA). The solutions were then desalted on PierceTM C-18 spin columns (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and eluted with 80% ACN and 0.1% TFA solvent. In preparation for liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS), the final eluted solutions were once again dried down and dissolved in 15 µl of 0.1% TFA in water. Liquid Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry Peptides were analysed using an UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled with a nano-electrospray ionization (nano-ESI) source (EASY-Spray NG ion source; Thermo Fisher Scientific), which was integrated with an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scentific). For the analysis, 1.8 µg of peptides were captured on a µ-Precolumn (Acclaim PepMap 100 C18 HPLC column, 300 µm × 5 mm, particle size 5 µm) and then separated on an EASY-Spray PepMap RSLC C18 column (Thermo Fisher Scientific) (150 μm × 15 cm, particle size 2 µm; Thermo Fisher Scientific). The mobile-phase flow rate was set to 300 nl/min. Peptides were eluted by mobile-phase A (0.1% formic acid in water, v/v) and mobile-phase B (0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile, v/v). The gradient profile was as follows: 0 min – 5% B; 22 min – 40% B; 23.1 min – 90% B; 25 min – 90% B; 25.1 min – 10% B; 30 min – 10% B. The eluted peptides were immediately ionized (1600 V, 275°C). Each full high-resolution spectrum was scanned using the Orbitrap analyser within a range of 350 to 2000 m/z at a resolution (R) of 120,000 and a maximum accumulation time of 50 ms. For MS/MS measurement, the data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode was used. Ions were isolated in a 1.6-Th window and fragmented by higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 30%. Precursor ions with charge states ranging from +2 to +8 were selected for fragmentation. MS/MS spectra were scanned using the Orbitrap analyser with automatic gain control (AGC) values set at 400,000 (MS) and 50,000 (MS/MS), R = 30,000. Dynamic exclusion was enabled with an exclusion duration of 10 s and an exclusion window of 10 ppm. All scans were collected in profile mode. Measurements were performed in triplicate for each sample containing an individual cross-linker or mixture of cross-linkers.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were converted to mascot generic format (MGF) using MSConvert (ver. 3.0.22045). The converted MGF files were then imported into MeroX software (ver. 2.0.1.4) to identify cross-linked peptides [17]. Parameters recommended by the MeroX producers were used. The sequence of mature BSA after cleavage of the signal peptide (UniProt entry P02769) was used as the database for the search in the case of BSA cross-linking, while the sequences of hemoglobin subunit alpha (UniProt entry P69905) and beta (UniProt entry P68871) were used in the case of hemoglobin cross-linking. Trypsin was selected as a protease with a maximum of three missed cleavage sites. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was used as a static modification and methionine oxidation as a variable modification. Peptides with a minimum length of 5 were included in the search. The lower mass limit was set to 100 Da and the upper mass limit  was set to 6000 Da, with a signal-to-noise ratio of 2.0. The ion types a, b and y were searched. The first linkable site was defined as the amino group of lysine (K) and the N-terminal amine group whereas the second linkable site included lysine (K), serine (S), threonine (T) and tyrosine (Y) [45]. The mass tolerance for precursor ions and fragmented ions was set to 5 ppm and 10 ppm, respectively. The results were filtered at a 5% false discovery rate (FDR) at the spectrum level, with a score cut-off of 50 . Acquired cross-links were manually inspected. For the DSSBU, which is structurally similar to DSBU and has the same mass difference (196.085 u) between two unmodified amino acids and a cross-linked amino acid, the same MeroX search parameters were applied. The cross-links identified in all three replicates of the same sample were merged and used for the cross-linkers comparison.
